prediction.likelyOutcome: Allied Development will almost certainly obtain a damages judgment against IGO and Carver jointly — liability is already locked in by partial summary judgment and the guaranty is unchallenged. The real fight at the ore tenus hearing is how much of the $146,910 claimed the court awards after crediting IGO's mitigation argument about the reletting; given the genuine factual dispute over whether the internal tenant relocation actually mitigated the loss (versus merely shifting the vacancy), a moderate-to-strong recovery somewhere well above tenant's $18,900 offer but meaningfully below the full $146,910 ceiling is the most probable outcome.

issues.label: Future/Accelerated Rent Claim Under Default Provision
Breach of Quiet Enjoyment / Constructive Eviction (Liability Defense)

outcome.description: After a damages hearing, the Baldwin Circuit Court rendered judgment for the landlord in the amount of $94,350 plus costs of court against the tenant and guarantor (the landlord had claimed $89,010 in its summary-judgment motion and later $146,910; the tenant argued for no more than $18,900). Attorney's fees were not separately stated. The Supreme Court of Alabama affirmed both the liability determination and the damages judgment.
